definition.title: R3 beam — controlled benchmark scenario
definition.hiddenTruth: Partner-reported chain: with rolls removed the raised assembly could exceed its normal installed-roll travel. The beam wedged against the spreader/posts while the yoke drifted down, displacing the link until it cleared the lifting point. Slow isolation-valve bleed-through was reported. Design and task isolation did not adequately address this configuration and gravity. Preserve the distinction between historical notification and controlled derivatives of partner findings. Original video, drawings, measurements and signed isolation records are not available. Never invent them or silently resolve the A/B hydraulic-system discrepancy.

sources.title: Initial incident description
sources.sourceClass: Historical notification excerpt supplied for this benchmark
sources.text: At approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2), the R3 Exit Carrier Beam at the Indiana Harbor 80 inch Hot Strip roughing mill fell from the yoke into the R3 mill pit, landing on the sled and a scaffold platform. No team members were in the pit. Contractor employees had worked there earlier, and two nearby contractors witnessed the fall. The beam and link were intact with the keeper installed; no damage was apparent on the yoke. A small top operator-side mill window liner fell with the beam. No relevant crane lift had occurred. Work rolls and top and bottom backup rolls were removed on the prior shift. The top backup roll balance was isolated raised; B hydraulics were shut off and bled.

sources.title: Outage configuration
sources.sourceClass: Controlled derivative of partner finding; not an original field record
sources.text: With work rolls and backup rolls absent, the raised assembly could reach a position beyond its usual installed-roll limit. The top backup roll balance remained isolated in the fully raised position.

sources.title: Reported video sequence
sources.sourceClass: Controlled derivative of partner-reported video finding; original video unavailable
sources.text: The beam became wedged against the top mill spreader and mill posts. The yoke drifted downward over approximately two hours while the wedged beam remained stationary. Relative movement displaced the link away from center until it cleared the yoke or lifting point. Exact displacement, forces, and the time of initial wedging are not established.

sources.title: Reported hydraulic findings
sources.sourceClass: Controlled derivative; raw valve tests and historian data unavailable
sources.text: The R3 isolation valve had reported slow bleed-through capable of allowing yoke drift after shutdown. Isolation valves were not routinely inspected and were replaced when found defective. Exact leak-down rate, pressure history, and pre-outage defect onset are not established. B hydraulics appear in the incident narrative, but A hydraulics appear in the causal chart; this discrepancy remains unresolved.

sources.title: Reported design findings
sources.sourceClass: Controlled derivative of partner design finding; controlled drawings unavailable
sources.text: The original design used one keeper on each link arm. No stop prevented beam wedging on the spreader or posts with backup rolls removed. Full drawing tolerances and clearance calculations are not available.

sources.title: Reported isolation findings
sources.sourceClass: Controlled derivative of partner RCA finding; signed execution records unavailable
sources.text: Gravity and stored energy were not fully accounted for in the task-specific isolation. Adequate positive mechanical restraint for the raised assembly was not established. This does not establish who authorized leaving the balance raised or whether any temporary restraint had been installed and later removed.

sources.title: Reported component condition
sources.sourceClass: Controlled derivative of partner findings; raw measurements unavailable
sources.text: The carrier beam weighed approximately 8,500 pounds. The beam and link were intact and the keeper remained installed. Measured wear did not provide enough normal clearance for release in the seated position. Raw dimensions and measurement methods are unavailable. The window liner’s causal role is not established.
